english: Let $A=\begin{pmatrix}\frac14&1\\[2pt]\frac{1}{16}&-\frac14\end{pmatrix}$ and let $I$ be the $2\times2$ identity matrix. For each positive integer $n$, let $S_n=I+A+A^{2}+\cdots+A^{n}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}$ (sum of all the entries of $S_n$) is ______.
hindi: माना कि $A=\begin{pmatrix}\frac14&1\\[2pt]\frac{1}{16}&-\frac14\end{pmatrix}$ है तथा $I$, $2\times2$ तत्समक आव्यूह है। प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए माना $S_n=I+A+A^{2}+\cdots+A^{n}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}$ ($S_n$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों का योग) का मान ______ है।
solution: So $A^{2k}=\dfrac{1}{8^{k}}I$ and $A^{2k+1}=\dfrac{1}{8^{k}}A$: the powers split into two GPs with ratio $\dfrac18$
solution_full: Compute $A^{2}$: the $(1,1)$ entry is $\frac{1}{16}+1\cdot\frac{1}{16}=\frac18$, the $(1,2)$ entry is $\frac14\cdot1+1\cdot\left(-\frac14\right)=0$, the $(2,1)$ entry is $\frac{1}{16}\cdot\frac14+\left(-\frac14\right)\frac{1}{16}=0$, and the $(2,2)$ entry is $\frac{1}{16}+\frac{1}{16}=\frac18$. So $A^{2}=\frac18I$.
The geometric series has ratio $\frac18$, so $\sum_{k=0}^{m}8^{-k}=\dfrac{1-8^{-(m+1)}}{1-\frac18}\to\dfrac87$.
Also $S_{2m}=S_{2m+1}-A^{2m+1}=S_{2m+1}-8^{-m}A$, and $8^{-m}A\to O$, so both subsequences have the same limit $\dfrac87(I+A)$.
Since the sum of entries is linear, the required limit is $\dfrac87\cdot\dfrac{49}{16}=\dfrac{7}{2}=3.50$.
originality_note: New: a matrix series I + A + A^2 + ... in which A^2 is a scalar matrix, so the series splits into two scalar GPs multiplying I and A (way 4, hidden structure). Closest known: sum of a GP of numbers, and (I - A)^{-1} as a matrix geometric series (not JEE). Different because: the trace-zero matrix with det -1/8 hides A^2 = (1/8) I, which turns a matrix series into a scalar GP.
blueprint_concepts: Higher integral powers of a square matrices

concept_use.Higher integral powers of a square matri: A^2 = (1/8) I gives every power: A^{2k} = 8^{-k} I and A^{2k+1} = 8^{-k} A.
concept_use.Geometric Progression (GP) & Sum of GP: The even and odd powers form geometric progressions with ratio 1/8, summed to infinity as 8/7.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy sums I + A + ... + A^199 (entry sum 3.5000000000) and gives A^2 = I/8; the limit 7/2 = 3.50 is a positive decimal as planned. Changed: wrote the limit of the sum of entries explicitly so the reading is unique.
key_step: Discovering A^2 = (1/8) I, then splitting the matrix series into two geometric progressions.
justification: Two linked ideas (a hidden scalar square and a GP sum with an even/odd split) in numerical format. Comparable to the sum-of-powers statement in 2026-P1-Q8 (L3).
